guideTitle: 5 Best Smart Bulbs Without a Hub (2026)
metaTitle: Best Smart Bulbs Without a Hub (2026)
metaDescription: Five Wi-Fi smart bulbs that need no hub, compared on brightness, Wi-Fi band support and voice control, so setup stays simple for any home.
introParagraphs: A hub is one more box to buy, plug in and troubleshoot, and many people would rather skip it. This guide compares five Wi-Fi smart bulbs that connect straight to your router, from the Lightinginside 100W pair that lists 1350 lumens to the Linkind Matter bulb that lists 1100 lumens and works on both 2.4G and 5G Wi-Fi.

The picks differ in brightness and compatibility. The Kasa KL135P2 lists 1000 lumens with whites from 2500K to 9000K, the Kasa KL125P4 is an 800 lumen, 9W bulb, the Philips WiZ pair is 800 lumens and the Lightinginside connects locally via Bluetooth or Wi-Fi. The Linkind stands out as the only one here that lists 5G support along with Matter.

We evaluated each bulb from its listing and buyer feedback, weighing how straightforward the no hub setup is, how much light it gives and how well it should hold a connection. Active adults and the family helping them will find a pick for a few lamps without a hub.

products.name: Linkind Matter Smart Bulbs, 5GHz Compatible
products.description:
The Linkind Matter bulb is the best no hub pick because it removes the most common setup headache: the 2.4GHz only rule. Its listing says it works on dual band Wi-Fi, 2.4G and 5G, which suits a crowded network. It lists 1100 lumens, brighter than the usual 800 lumen bulb.

It is also Matter enabled and works with Alexa, Apple Home and Google, so you are not tied to one speaker. The color temperature range of 1000K to 20000K is unusually wide, from candlelight to bright white. The tradeoff is that it carries the highest cost in this guide, and the very wide range is more than most people use.

Setup is a screw in and a scan with your chosen app. Leave the switch on so it keeps power. Compared with the Kasa KL135P2, it adds Matter and 5G, while the Kasa has a more established app.
products.bestFor: Busy home networks that want Matter and 5G support with no hub
pros: Matter works with Alexa, Apple and Google
cons: Range is wider than most people need

products.name: Kasa Smart Light Bulbs KL135P2, 1000 Lumens
products.description:
The Kasa KL135P2 is the strongest pick for people who want a bright, flexible Wi-Fi bulb with a familiar app. It lists 1000 lumens and whites from 2500K up to 9000K, plus 16 million colors. An auto white setting can adjust color temperature through the day.

The Kasa app on iOS and Android lets you dim, turn on and off or schedule from anywhere, and voice control works through Alexa or Google Assistant. The tradeoff is that it is not listed as Matter and the 1000 lumen output is below the Lightinginside's 1350. It also needs the Kasa app for setup.

Setup is quick and no hub is needed. A pair covers two lamps. Choose it over the KL125P4 for more light, and the Linkind for Matter.
products.bestFor: Kitchens and living rooms that need brighter light and a trusted app
cons: Not listed as a Matter bulb
Less bright than the 1350 lumen option

products.name: Kasa Multicolor Smart Bulb KL125P4
products.description:
The Kasa KL125P4 is the standard everyday bulb for a no hub home. It lists 800 lumens at 9W, full color and the free Kasa app. Voice control works through Alexa or Google Assistant.

Its Away Mode is a useful feature, since it can vary lights when you travel. The tradeoff is that it is dimmer than the KL135P2 and lacks Matter. It also needs the Kasa app for setup.

Setup is a screw in and app pairing, with nothing else to buy. It suits bedrooms and ordinary lamps. Choose it over the Philips WiZ if you prefer the Kasa app.
products.bestFor: Everyday lamps where voice control and Away Mode matter
pros: Away Mode varies lights when away
cons: Not listed as a Matter bulb

products.name: PHILIPS WiZ Color A19 Smart Bulbs, 2 Pack
products.description:
The Philips WiZ pair connects straight to your router and adds features no other bulb here has. SpaceSense lets the bulb detect motion and turn on automatically, which suits a hallway. You can also use the WiZ app, the WiZ remote or voice commands to Alexa, Google Home or Siri.

It offers 16 million colors and warm to cool whites, with schedules. The tradeoff is that it needs the WiZ app and its 800 lumens is modest. It does not list Matter.

Setup is a screw in and a Wi-Fi join in the app. A pair covers two lamps. Compared with the Kasa KL125P4, it adds motion and a remote.
products.bestFor: Hallways and bathrooms where motion based lighting helps

products.name: Lightinginside 100W Smart Bulbs, 2 Pack
products.description:
The Lightinginside pair is the brightest here at 1350 lumens, equal to a 100W bulb, from only 11W. That suits stairs, kitchens and workshops. It pairs through the free SmartLife app via Wi-Fi and works with Alexa and Google Assistant.

It can connect locally via Bluetooth or Wi-Fi and offers remote control when away. The tradeoff is that the brand and app are less familiar, and it does not list Matter. A 100W equivalent bulb may not suit every fixture.

Setup is a screw in and app pairing. A pair covers two bright spots. Pick it for brightness, and the Kasa KL135P2 for a better known app.
products.bestFor: Large rooms and workspaces that need the most light

buyingCriteria.explanation: Wi-Fi bulbs usually need a 2.4 GHz network, and joining 5 GHz is a common setup failure. The Linkind lists support for both 2.4G and 5G, which helps on a crowded router. The Kasa and Lightinginside bulbs are 2.4G class. Check which band your phone uses during setup.

buyingCriteria.criterion: How many bulbs without a hub
buyingCriteria.explanation: A no hub system is simple for a few lamps, but hub based Zigbee or Thread systems feel more reliable beyond about 10 to 15 lights. The Philips WiZ and Kasa pairs suit a few lamps. Each Wi-Fi bulb joins your router, which adds load. Plan a hub if you expect a whole house.

A standard A19 is about 800 lumens, and brighter models run 1,100 to 1,600 lumens. The Linkind lists 1100, the Kasa KL135P2 lists 1000 and the Lightinginside lists 1350. The KL125P4 and Philips WiZ list 800. Choose brighter bulbs for kitchens and stairs.

Matter needs both bulb and controller to be Matter certified. The Linkind is Matter and works with Alexa, Apple and Google. The Kasa and Lightinginside bulbs are not listed as Matter. Choose Matter if you may change speakers.

With no hub, the app is your control center. The Kasa app is established, the WiZ app adds a remote option and SmartLife is generic. A steady app avoids dropped schedules. Read reviews on the app, not just the bulb.
A smart bulb needs constant power, so a switch off kills control. After an outage some bulbs return at full brightness. Leave switches on. Check the power on setting.

cards.text: The Kasa KL125P4 is the easiest to live with. The Linkind is the pick if your router is dual band.

faq.q: Do smart bulbs need a hub?
faq.a: Wi-Fi smart bulbs such as these do not need a hub. They connect directly to your router. A hub helps beyond many lights.

faq.q: How much do no hub smart bulbs cost?
faq.a: The Lightinginside is the lowest cost here and the Linkind sits higher. Packs change the per bulb cost. Check current prices on Amazon.

faq.q: Why will my bulb not join Wi-Fi?
faq.a: Most bulbs need 2.4 GHz, and a 5 GHz network is the usual cause. The Linkind lists dual band support. Move closer to the router and retry.

faq.q: Can I control the bulb away from home?
faq.a: Yes, through Wi-Fi remote control in the app. The Kasa app does this on iOS and Android. Away Mode on the KL125P4 varies lights.

faq.q: Is Matter the same as no hub?
faq.a: No, Matter is a standard that works across platforms. A bulb can be no hub and not Matter. The Linkind is both.

faq.q: What happens after a power cut?
faq.a: Some bulbs return at full brightness. Check the power on setting. This matters at night.

faq.q: How long do these bulbs last?
faq.a: LED bulbs generally last many years. App support may age sooner. Check each warranty.
